questions.stem: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, what mass of magnesium oxide is produced when 4.8 g of magnesium reacts completely? [Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Step 1: Moles of Mg = 4.8 / 24 = 0.2 mol. Step 2: From the equation, 2 mol Mg produces 2 mol MgO (1:1 ratio), so 0.2 mol Mg produces 0.2 mol MgO. Step 3: Mr of MgO = 24 + 16 = 40. Mass of MgO = 0.2 x 40 = 8.0 g.

questions.stem: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. What mass of calcium oxide (CaO) is produced from 25 g of calcium carbonate? [Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of CaCO₃ = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100. Moles of CaCO₃ = 25/100 = 0.25 mol. From the equation, 1 mol CaCO₃ produces 1 mol CaO. Mr of CaO = 40 + 16 = 56. Mass of CaO = 0.25 x 56 = 14 g. Alternatively, the CO₂ lost = 0.25 x 44 = 11 g. Check: 14 + 11 = 25 g (conservation of mass).

questions.stem: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. What mass of hydrogen gas is produced when 4.6 g of sodium reacts with excess water? [Ar: Na = 23, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Moles of Na = 4.6 / 23 = 0.2 mol. From the equation: 2 mol Na produces 1 mol H₂ (2:1 ratio). So 0.2 mol Na produces 0.1 mol H₂. Mr of H₂ = 2 x 1 = 2. Mass of H₂ = 0.1 x 2 = 0.2 g. The key step is using the molar ratio from the balanced equation (2:1).

questions.stem: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. What mass of iron can be obtained from 320 g of iron(III) oxide? [Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of Fe₂O₃ = (2 x 56) + (3 x 16) = 112 + 48 = 160. Moles of Fe₂O₃ = 320/160 = 2 mol. From the equation: 1 mol Fe₂O₃ produces 2 mol Fe. So 2 mol Fe₂O₃ produces 4 mol Fe. Mass of Fe = 4 x 56 = 224 g.

questions.stem: What mass of oxygen is needed to react completely with 6 g of carbon in the reaction C + O₂ → CO₂? [Ar: C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Moles of C = 6/12 = 0.5 mol. From the equation: 1 mol C requires 1 mol O₂ (1:1 ratio). So 0.5 mol C requires 0.5 mol O₂. Mr of O₂ = 32. Mass of O₂ = 0.5 x 32 = 16 g. Check by conservation of mass: 6 g C + 16 g O₂ = 22 g CO₂ (0.5 x 44 = 22 g).
